summary: Signup Sheets lets you post what an event needs — dishes to bring, roles to serve, shifts to cover — and lets people claim those slots themselves, either inside ChurchCRM or through a public share link.

sections.title: Getting Started
sections.content:
1. Open **Events > Signup Sheets** and choose **New Sheet**
2. Give the sheet a title, and optionally attach it to an existing church event
3. Add a slot for each thing you need — "Bring a dessert", "Greeter, 9:00 service", "Stack chairs after"
4. Set the capacity on each slot: how many people (or dishes) you need. Use 0 for unlimited
5. Set the sheet status to **Open** so people can start claiming slots

sections.title: Slots and Categories
sections.content:
Give slots a category to group them on the page — for example Food, Setup, Cleanup, or a service time. Slots without a category appear together at the top.

Enable **Allow quantity** on a slot when one person might cover several units of it, such as "Bring a dozen cookies" where someone can bring three dozen.

sections.title: Public Share Links
sections.content:
Switch a sheet to public and it gets a secret link at `/external/signup-sheets/{token}`. Anyone with the link can claim a slot by entering their name and email — no CRM login required.

The link is unguessable but not private: treat it as shareable with your congregation, not as a secret. Turn public sharing off for a sheet at any time and the link stops working immediately.

Each volunteer gets their own manage link after signing up so they can cancel without contacting you.

sections.title: Managing Signups
sections.content:
Open a sheet to see who has claimed what. You can add a signup on someone's behalf, remove a signup, and export the whole roster as CSV for printing or emailing.

When a signup is linked to a Person record, the roster shows the CRM name; public signups show the name the volunteer typed.

sections.title: Privacy & Abuse Protection
sections.content:
Public sheets accept a limited number of signups per hour from any one visitor — adjustable in plugin settings. Signup attempts are recorded with a hashed IP address only; no raw addresses are stored.

Public pages list volunteers by name so people can see who has already claimed a slot. Email addresses and phone numbers are never shown there — those are visible only to logged-in CRM users.
